Content: Peregrine falcons are an endangered species in New York State. This crow-sized predator feeds primarily on birds. Starting in the `text(1940s)`, exposure to the pesticide DDT in their prey caused declines in the peregrine falcon population. These pesticides caused eggshell thinning, which drastically lowered breeding success. By the `text(early 1960s)`, peregrine falcons no longer nested in New York State. After the United States banned DDT in `1972`, efforts were made to reintroduce peregrine falcons into the Northeast. Since the `text(1980s)`, the peregrine falcons are `text(once)` again breeding in many areas of New York State.
